title: Runtime security: privileges, capabilities and a read-only filesystem

videos.script: Shelf no longer runs as root. A container still gets more than it needs, and this lesson takes the rest away. {{caps}} Root in a container holds fourteen capabilities by default. Shelf needs none of them, so it gets none. {{privileged}} Then two flags that undo every wall: privileged, and the Docker socket mounted inside. Ana learns to recognise them, and writes a short script that finds them on a machine. {{readonly}} Last, a filesystem nobody can write to. Shelf runs that way unchanged. Postgres needs two small places to write, and its own log says which.
